problem_interpretation: Design a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (refractive index 1.52, lossless) with air incidence (index 1.0). The design must use exactly one layer of lossless SiO2 (n=1.46) and one layer of lossless TiO2 (n=2.40) in either stacking order. Each layer thickness is constrained between 40 nm and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence, sampled from 450 nm to 700 nm in 5 nm steps. A mean reflectance below 0.03 is the stated performance target. The method must use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) only, excluding RCWA, FDFD, learned surrogates, or hardware acceleration. The process allows at most two research rounds with one route and up to 64 solver evaluations per round using seed 17. Decisions to adjust or stop must be based on observed results and independent numeric checks.

route_summaries.scientific_hypothesis: A stacking order with the lower-index material (SiO2) facing the incident medium and the higher-index material (TiO2) adjacent to the glass substrate allows for a broader spectral suppression of reflectance within the 40-160 nm thickness constraints than the reverse order, potentially achieving a mean reflectance below 0.03.
route_summaries.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) optimization for a planar stack consisting of Air (n=1.0), followed by a SiO2 (Gao) layer (lossless, constant n=1.46), followed by a TiO2 (Siefke) layer (lossless, constant n=2.40), on a semi-infinite Glass substrate (lossless, constant n=1.52). The design variables are the thickness of the SiO2 (Gao) layer and the thickness of the TiO2 (Siefke) layer, both constrained to the range [40, 160] nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees), sampled at 5 nm intervals from 450 nm to 700 nm. Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Allow up to 64 solver evaluations. Report the best found thickness pair, the resulting reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Do not use RCWA, FDFD, or surrogate models.

route_summaries.route_title: Strictly Bounded Two-Layer AR Optimization with Corrected Budget
route_summaries.scientific_hypothesis: A two-layer stack comprising one SiO2 and one TiO2 layer, with thicknesses bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm, can achieve an arithmetic mean reflectance below 0.03 across the 450-700 nm band at normal incidence if the optimizer finds a non-quarter-wave thickness combination that balances the spectral ripple, or if the optimal solution lies near the quarter-wave points (~98 nm for SiO2, ~60 nm for TiO2) adjusted for broadband performance.

## Problem interpretation

Design a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (refractive index 1.52, lossless) with air incidence (index 1.0). The design must use exactly one layer of lossless SiO2 (n=1.46) and one layer of lossless TiO2 (n=2.40) in either stacking order. Each layer thickness is constrained between 40 nm and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence, sampled from 450 nm to 700 nm in 5 nm steps. A mean reflectance below 0.03 is the stated performance target. The method must use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) only, excluding RCWA, FDFD, learned surrogates, or hardware acceleration. The process allows at most two research rounds with one route and up to 64 solver evaluations per round using seed 17. Decisions to adjust or stop must be based on observed results and independent numeric checks.
